candidates.heading: PrimeTime DUPR League Key Dates
candidates.content:
PrimeTime DUPR League Key Dates
• Sept. 7, Monday – Open Registration
• Sept. 27, Sunday – Season DUPR ratings recorded
• Sept. 28, Monday - Can start updating rosters
• Oct. 4, Sunday – Last day to register (4 weeks)
• Oct. 7, Wednesday – Schedules completed and sent
• Oct. 16 - PrimeTime League Starts
• Nov. 25/26 Break Week
• Dec. 4 - PrimeTime League Regular Season Ends
• Dec. 11 - PrimeTime League Championship Day
Note: No games the week of Nov. 22 (Thanksgiving Break)

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
candidates.content:
6.3. PrimeTime DUPR League
The PrimeTime DUPR League is exclusively for players age 65 and older who want
competitive play against others in the same age group. Using DUPR's 65+ age-based rating
system, the league provides a more level playing field by matching players of similar age and
ability. Separate men's and women's divisions compete weekly with two doubles teams
representing each squad, and any tied team match is decided by the exciting Picklebreaker
format. PrimeTime emphasizes spirited competition, sportsmanship, and the opportunity
for experienced players to continue enjoying high-quality league play in a community-
focused environment.

candidates.heading: CLUB LEAGUE FORMAT
candidates.content:
1. CLUB LEAGUE FORMAT
1.1. Club main website: https://lwrpickleballclub.com
1.2. League Management System (LMS) website: https://league.lwrpickleballclub.com
1.3. There are three seasons: Fall, Winter, and Spring.
1.4. Each season consists of a multi-week regular play followed by championships/playoƯs.
1.5. League teams are divided by Divisions based on DUPR ratings.
1.6. The Leagues consist of:
1.6.1. Weekday DUPR League – Gender doubles scheduled play during the week
1.6.2. Saturday League - Gender Doubles/Mixed play using the Picklebreaker™ format
(every other Saturday)
1.6.3. PrimeTime League – Gender doubles, aged 65+ scheduled play on Fridays

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
candidates.heading: Match Day Format
candidates.content:
6.2.3. Match Day Format: (See table below)
6.2.3.1. All Games: Games to 15 using Rally Scoring* (win by 1). 1 point per win. Two
one-minute timeouts per team/game but no timeouts in Picklebreaker. Teams
switch ends when the first team reaches 8 points. Visitors choose serve,
receive, side, or defer in games 1 and 3 and all mixed games.
6.2.3.2. Men's Round Robin: 3 Men’s teams play Round Robin (from low to high,
Teams 1 to 3). Each player will play 3 games. 9 points possible.
6.2.3.3. Women's Round Robin: 3 Women’s teams play Round Robin (from low to
high, Teams 4 to 6). Each player will play 3 games. 9 points possible.
6.2.3.4. Mixed Round: Create 6 Mixed teams (from low to high, Teams 7 to 12). Each
player will play 1 mixed game. 6 points possible.
6.2.3.5. Picklebreaker™ Game (Only played if tie at the end of all previous rounds -
12-12): Features all the mixed teams that played in the Mixed rounds. This will

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
candidates.heading: Scoring
candidates.content:
6.3.4. Scoring: Each standard round win earns 1 point, with a maximum of 5 total
possible match points per date. If the regular round-robin ends in a tie (2-2), a
Picklebreaker will be played, awarding 1 extra bonus point to the winner. If there is
no tie, the outright winning team receives the 1-point bonus.
6.3.5. Player Cap: Each player plays 4 games with a possible 6+ games.

candidates.heading: 21.A Standard Time-Out — Between Games
candidates.content:
21.A.3 Between Games. Between games, players may request to use
one or both standard time-outs before the start of the next
game. The players must inform the referee. The standard time-
out will start immediately after the expiration of the time-out
between games. A time-out must be charged when any portion
of the time is used. When the requesting singles player or
doubles team is ready to resume play before a requested time-
out begins, that time-out is not charged.

candidates.heading: The Game
candidates.content:
Section 1 The Game
Pickleball is a paddle sport that combines elements of badminton, table
tennis, and tennis. It is played using a special perforated ball on a 20-foot
by 44-foot court with a tennis type net. The court is divided into right and
left service courts and a non-volley zone on each end of the net (Figure 3-1).
Pickleball can be played as singles or doubles.
In standard pickleball, the ball is served diagonally across the net to the
opposite service court on the opponent’s end, using an approved motion.
The ball is then hit back and forth across the net until a player fails to return
the ball in accordance with the rules.
Standard pickleball uses a scoring method where points are scored only
when the serving team wins the rally. The server alternates service courts
and continues to serve until they lose a rally (commit a fault). Typically, the
first player or team scoring 11 points and leading by at least a 2-point
margin wins the game.
Rally scoring has been provisionally approved as an option (Rule 14.A),
wherein a point is scored by the team that wins each rally. Mini-singles
(Rule 14.B) is a half-court variation of standard singles.
Unique Features
Two-Bounce Rule. After the serve, the receiver must allow the ball to
bounce before making their first return, and then the serving team must
allow the ball to bounce before making their first return.
Non-Volley Zone. The non-volley zone is the area of the court that
extends 7 feet from the net on each end of the court, within which a player
is not allowed to hit the ball out of the air before it bounces.
Wheelchair and Adaptive Play. Players using wheelchairs and players
having certain disabilities may allow the ball to bounce twice before
returning the ball. The first bounce must be in the court, but the second

candidates.heading: End Change Time-Out
candidates.content:
21.B End Change Time-Out. The referee will call a time-out to allow players to
change ends at specified points during single-game matches and tie-
breaker games. Players will not change ends during the tie-breaker game
when the first game of the match was forfeited due to late arrival.
21.B.1 11-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 11
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 6.
21.B.2 15-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 15
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 8.
21.B.3 21-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 21
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 11.

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
candidates.content:
6.1.9.7. The Picklebreaker™ shall be played only when the match is tied 2–2
following completion of all preceding rounds. The Picklebreaker™ features the
designated doubles teams that participated in the preceding rounds, rotating
in accordance with the Picklebreaker™ Rotation Rules. The Picklebreaker™
shall consist of one game to 15 points, win by two (2), using Rally Scoring.
Note: Picklebreaker matches will not be recorded in DUPR and do not reflect
on individual’s W/L record.

candidates.heading: 21.D Referee Time-Out — Resuming Play
candidates.content:
21.D.4 Resuming Play. The referee will resume play by announcing a
15-second warning (Rule 17.D.16).

candidates.heading: 15.B Event Formats — Double Elimination
candidates.content:
15.B.1 Double Elimination. In a double elimination format, after losing
one match, a singles player or doubles team plays in a consolation
bracket. The player or team is eliminated from competition after
one loss in the consolation bracket. The winner of the consolation
bracket plays the winner of the winners’ bracket to determine first
place and second place. If the winner of the consolation bracket
defeats the winner of the winners’ bracket, then a tie-breaker
match to 15 points must be played to determine first place and
second place. The loser of the final match in the consolation
bracket wins third place.

candidates.heading: Extending Time to Report to Match
candidates.content:
16.M Extending Time to Report to Match. The Tournament Director may allow
an extension of time for players to report to a match when circumstances
warrant.

candidates.heading: 21.F Time-Out Between Games — Resuming Play
candidates.content:
21.F.4 Resuming Play. The referee will resume play by announcing a
15-second warning (Rule 17.D.16).

Entering Match Scores
Captains enter scores, record forfeits, and confirm official match results. When entering
scores, normally select the “Use this saved team” pulldown to display the previously
entered Match Setup team. If there were changes to that, simply select the correct player in
the individual player pulldown option.
• Game Forfeits & Retirements: Refer to the official League Rules when entering
results for individual games impacted by player or play-related issues.
• Full Match Cancellations: If an entire match date is forfeited or cannot be played
due to weather or scheduling conflicts, do not enter it into the system. Instead,
contact League Management at info@lwrpickleballclub.com.
• Eligible/Ineligible Player: In actual score entry, the same eligibility rules apply to
the players entered for each game line. An ineligible player cannot be selected, and
score fields are blocked if that line has an eligibility issue.
